newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Curacao oil refinery sees 170,000 bpd on Aug 22.
newsitem.headline: Curacao oil refinery sees 170,000 bpd on Aug 22.

text.p: The fire-striken Curacao oil refinery, operated by Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA), expects to increase crude throughput by 65,000 barrels per day (bpd) on August 22 to 170,000 bpd, a senior refinery official said on Tuesday.
The refinery was hit by a serious fire last Thursday which disabled its main crude processing unit.

The unit would be partially repaired by August 22 and ready to handle 115,000 bpd, the official said. This, added to 55,000 bpd processing in the refinery's undamaged crude unit, would bring crude runs to 170,000 bpd in the last week of August.
The refinery was currently running 105,000 bpd, using the undamaged crude unit and a thermal cracker converted for use as a crude distiller.
In July, the refinery processed an average of 192,000 bpd of crude oil.
The official said maintenance of the undamaged unit, which had been scheduled for August, would now probably occur in September.
Full repairs of the main crude processing unit, which has the capacity to process 180,000 bpd, would take another six weeks from the end of August, he added.
The refinery is rented by PDVSA on a 20-year contract and is a major supplier of refined products to the U.S. market.
